description: Open quick help from an empty prompt; press again to dismiss it and insert a literal question mark.
when_to_use: Use when you need an in-session reminder of commands or shortcuts.

name: Esc
description: Cancel the current operation; press twice to interrupt a running turn or stop background agents while the main agent is idle.
when_to_use: Use when the active operation or turn should stop.

name: Ctrl+C
description: Cancel the active operation or clear input; press twice to exit.

examples.explanation: Cancel work or clear the current input.

when_to_use: Use for terminal-standard interruption and exit behavior.

name: Ctrl+D
description: Shut down the Copilot CLI process.
when_to_use: Use when the interactive CLI should close cleanly.

name: Ctrl+G
description: Open the current prompt in the editor configured by the EDITOR environment variable.

examples.explanation: Edit a long prompt in the configured external editor.

when_to_use: Use for a long or structured prompt that is awkward to edit on one terminal line.

name: Ctrl+L
description: Clear the terminal display without ending the session.

examples.explanation: Clear visual clutter while keeping the session active.

when_to_use: Use when you want a clean terminal view without clearing conversation context.

name: Ctrl+Q
description: Queue the current input to run after the agent's active task finishes.

examples.explanation: Queue the typed follow-up while Copilot is busy.

when_to_use: Use when you want a follow-up, shell command, or supported slash command to run in order after current work.

conditions: The agent must be running for the input to be queued.

name: Ctrl+R
description: Reverse-search prior command and prompt input.

examples.explanation: Find and reuse a previous prompt from input history.

when_to_use: Use when repeating or adapting a prompt entered earlier.

name: Ctrl+V
description: Paste clipboard content into the prompt as an attachment.

examples.explanation: Attach clipboard content to the current prompt.

when_to_use: Use when clipboard content should be supplied as explicit prompt context.

conditions: Requires clipboard integration in the terminal environment.

name: Alt+V
description: Paste an image from the clipboard into the prompt as an attachment.

examples.explanation: Attach a clipboard screenshot to the prompt.

when_to_use: Use when a screenshot or diagram is useful context for the task.

conditions: Requires clipboard image support and a model and organization policy that allow vision input.

name: Ctrl+X then /
display_name: Run a slash command while drafting
description: Run a slash command after prompt text has already been entered without retyping the draft.

examples.explanation: Change the model while preserving the prompt currently being drafted.

when_to_use: Use when a session setting needs to change after you have started composing a prompt.

conditions: Prompt input must already contain text.

name: Ctrl+X then b
description: Promote the running task or shell command to background execution.

examples.explanation: Move a long-running test command to the background and continue interacting.

when_to_use: Use when active work can continue while a task or shell command finishes.

conditions: A task or shell command must be running.

name: Shift+Enter
description: Insert a newline into prompt input instead of submitting it.

examples.explanation: Add another line to a structured prompt without sending it.

when_to_use: Use to compose multiline requirements or checklists in the prompt box.

conditions: On macOS Option+Enter is also supported; on Windows and Linux Alt+Enter is supported.
